method: Each claim checked against the retrieved abstract text of its cited source, not against the citation. Numbers compared digit by digit. A claim the source text does not state is marked fail regardless of whether it is true.
below_bar: The programme primer specifies a duopoly: two model families of different lineages. This is one verifier with no calibrated error rate.

claims.claim: Scope: non-pregnant, non-catheterised, no urological abnormality, not immunocompromised, no systemic illness or pyelonephritis
claims.source_text: a bacterial infection of the lower urinary tract with no sign of systemic illness or pyelonephritis in a noncatheterized, nonpregnant adult with no urologic abnormalities or immunocompromise

claims.claim: Typical symptoms without vaginal discharge diagnose without further testing
claims.source_text: a self-diagnosis of a UTI with the presence of typical symptoms ... without vaginal discharge, is accurate enough to diagnose an uncomplicated UTI without further testing

claims.claim: Culture reserved for recurrence, failure, resistant history, atypical presentation
claims.source_text: should be reserved for women with recurrent infection, treatment failure, history of resistant isolates, or atypical presentation

claims.claim: NSAIDs and delayed antibiotics an option; complication risk low
claims.source_text: Symptomatic treatment with nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs and delayed antibiotics may be considered because the risk of complications is low

claims.claim: Fluids, cranberry, methenamine hippurate prevent recurrence
claims.source_text: Increased fluids, intake of cranberry products, and methenamine hippurate can prevent recurrent infections

claims.claim: Men: always treat, culture-guided, seven days, consider urethritis/prostatitis
claims.source_text: Men with lower UTI symptoms should always receive antibiotics, with urine culture and susceptibility results guiding the antibiotic choice ... first-line antibiotics for men ... for seven days

claims.claim: Age >=65 non-frail: agents and durations unchanged, culture advised
claims.source_text: first-line antibiotics and treatment durations do not differ from those recommended for younger adults

claims.claim: Nitrofurantoin 5d 70% vs single-dose fosfomycin 58%, difference 12% (95% CI 4-21), P=.004
claims.source_text: Clinical resolution through day 28 was achieved in 171 of 244 patients (70%) receiving nitrofurantoin vs 139 of 241 patients (58%) receiving fosfomycin (difference, 12% [95% CI, 4%-21%]; P = .004)

claims.claim: Microbiological resolution 74% vs 63%
claims.source_text: Microbiologic resolution occurred in 129 of 175 (74%) vs 103 of 163 (63%)

claims.claim: SCOUT n=768, nitrofurantoin 74% highest, single-dose fosfomycin 59% lowest, difference 15.5pp (95% CI 5.9-25.1), p=0.0168
claims.source_text: 768 patients were randomly allocated ... nitrofurantoin had the highest (128 [74%] of 172 patients; difference 15.5 percentage points [95% CI 5.9 to 25.1] vs single-dose fosfomycin; p=0.0168)

claims.claim: SCOUT: pivmecillinam 70%, two-dose fosfomycin 67%
claims.source_text: pivmecillinam (127 [70%] of 182 ...) and the two-dose fosfomycin group (122 [67%] of 181

claims.claim: SCOUT authors: fosfomycin's first-line role should be re-evaluated
claims.source_text: The role of fosfomycin as a first-line antibiotic for uncomplicated UTI should be re-evaluated

claims.claim: AU: nitrofurantoin resistance 2.7%, trimethoprim 20.7%, ampicillin 41.9%
claims.source_text: Five-year hospital and community resistance rates were highest for ampicillin (41.9%) and trimethoprim (20.7%). Resistance was lowest for meropenem (0.0%), nitrofurantoin (2.7%)

claims.claim: S4 authors: ampicillin and trimethoprim should be reconsidered for empirical treatment
claims.source_text: these antimicrobials should be reconsidered for empirical treatment of UTIs in this patient population

claims.claim: S4: 5,333 first E. coli UTIs, 84.2% community-acquired, Canberra, 2009-2013
claims.source_text: Results are based on 5333 first E. coli UTIs ... of which 84.2% were community-acquired ... Canberra, Australia ... from 2009 to 2013

claims.claim: Adults: prior antibiotics within a year, OR 4.97 (95% CI 2.04-12.06)
claims.source_text: Antibiotic treatment within the last year was independently associated with antibiotic resistant E.coli in the urine sample adjusted OR 4.97 (95% CI 2.04-12.06)

claims.claim: Swedish primary care: 80% of E. coli susceptible to all tested; ciprofloxacin resistance lower than the laboratory reported
claims.source_text: A total of 80% of detected E.coli isolates were susceptible to all tested antimicrobials and resistance rates to ciprofloxacin were lower than reported from the local clinical laboratory

claims.claim: Children: prior antibiotics OR 13.23 (95% CI 7.84-22.31), persisting up to six months
claims.source_text: more likely to be resistant to antibiotics, and this increased risk could persist for up to six months (odds ratio 13.23, 95% confidence interval 7.84 to 22.31)

claims.claim: Audit and feedback raised first-line nitrofurantoin prescribing, OR 1.28 (95% CI 1.07-1.52)
claims.source_text: increased the relative probability of prescribing nitrofurantoin as first-line treatment for uncomplicated lower UTI by 28% (OR 1.28; 95% CI 1.07 to 1.52)

claims.claim: 24.0% one antibiotic allergy, 6.7% two or more, most common SXT 15.7%, n=375
claims.source_text: 375 participants completed the questionnaire ... 24.0% reporting 1 antibiotic allergy and 6.7% reporting >=2 antibiotic allergies. The most common allergy was to SXT (15.7%)

claims.claim: Nitrofurantoin and trimethoprim PBS-listed unrestricted; fosfomycin and pivmecillinam not on Schedule 4333
claims.source_text: Queried directly against PBS Public API v3 items, schedule 4333: Nitrofurantoin 4 rows benefit type U; Trimethoprim 23 rows U/R/S; Cefalexin 58 rows U/S; Fosfomycin no rows; Pivmecillinam no rows.

claims.claim: Clinical failure of 5-day nitrofurantoin rises as eGFR falls, aOR 1.05 per 10 mL/min (95% CI 1.01-1.09)
claims.source_text: Adjusted odds ratios for clinical failure per 10mL/min decrease in eGFR were 1.05 (95% CI: 1.01-1.09) for NF5

claims.claim: eGFR >=60: nitrofurantoin 14.6% failure vs fosfomycin 20.7%, trimethoprim 20.8%
claims.source_text: clinical failures occurred in 14.6% (1895/12 980) of NF5-treated, 20.7% (266/1283) of FT1-treated ... and 20.8% (66/318) of TMP3-treated patients

claims.claim: eGFR <60: fosfomycin 16.0% vs nitrofurantoin 23.3%, aOR 0.61 (95% CI 0.39-0.95)
claims.source_text: In uncomplicated cystitis and eGFR <60 mL/min, FT1 resulted in 16.0% (39/244) and NF5 in 23.3% clinical failures (110/472), aOR: 0.61, 95% CI: 0.39-0.95

claims.claim: Reduced GFR lowers urinary concentration while raising hepatic exposure two- to three-fold
claims.source_text: the liver of individuals with a moderate-to-severe glomerular filtration rate (GFR) is exposed to two-to-three-fold higher concentrations of NFT than individuals with a normal GFR, which coincided with a substantial reduction in the NFT urinary concentration

claims.claim: At eGFR <60, nitrofurantoin had lower odds of AKI hospitalisation than trimethoprim (aOR 0.62, 95% CI 0.40-0.94 at 45-59; 0.45, 95% CI 0.25-0.81 at <30), no greater odds of any adverse outcome; n=795,484
claims.source_text: 795,484 patients from 393 general practices ... Compared to trimethoprim, nitrofurantoin prescribing was associated with lower odds of hospitalisation for AKI (ORs ranged from 0.62 [95% CI 0.40-0.94], for eGFRs of 45-59, to 0.45 [95% CI 0.25-0.81] for eGFRs <30). Nitrofurantoin was not associated with greater odds of any adverse outcome

claims.claim: The contraindication below CrCl 60 rests on no supporting data
claims.source_text: Data supporting the contraindication of nitrofurantoin for patients with a CrCl less than 60 mL/min are nonexistent

claims.claim: Nitrofurantoin contraindicated below eGFR/CrCl 60 mL/min/1.73m2
claims.note: Reviewer attestation, not a literature claim. Concordant with the labelled contraindication; the literature basis is contested (S13, S12) while the efficacy basis is supported (S10, S11). Requires Dr Ken Lee's named sign-off to move from pending to attested.

claims.claim: Nitrofurantoin 100 mg three times daily for five days
claims.source_text: oral nitrofurantoin, 100 mg 3 times a day for 5 days (n = 255)
claims.note: Dose quoted from the trial regimen, not from an Australian product information. AU dosing listed as unresolved.
